title: Statewide serving sweep
status: HONEST PARTIAL CLOSE — instrument built and validated, two counties swept end to end, statewide address question settled at source; 252 counties not swept and the report says so
missionPremise: OPS-16 amendment A-018 (2026-08-18) opened P-43 as a sweep of what the product SERVES, explicitly distinct from the County Manifest's did-a-writer-run question, after the operator REFUSED a golden-parcel regression set because sampling narrowed scope on Bastrop and certified a broken county once. The lane's opening contradiction: P-27 records situs as 99.3% populated while the operator has missing addresses on single-family parcels in Bastrop (48021:36521 = 1503 Farm St on the CAD roll) and Travis (17005 Simsbrook Dr, Pflugerville). Both cannot be true.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (1) run `node --import tsx packages/retrieval/scripts/serving-sweep.mjs --county <fips> --out <dir>` against the two production stores and get a CountyServingSweep conforming to the planner's frozen record for every parcel on that county's roster with no sampling; (2) verify the sweep measures SERVED truth by running `npx vitest run src/serving-sweep/__tests__/live-parity.test.ts`, which compares the offline composition against captured DEPLOYED wire bodies; and (3) read a dated report that answers the 99.3% question with its denominator and counting rule. All three hold today.
scopeBasis: The dispatch required ONE county end to end before scoping waves, and the standing L2 lesson is that blockers surface serially. Bastrop was swept first (the operator's example, the most-warmed jurisdiction), then Travis (the second confirmed address gap, a different pipeline). Travis then invalidated the instrument's own address predicate, which is precisely the serial-blocker shape, so the lane STOPPED at two counties and reported rather than launching a 254-county wave on a predicate validated against one county's failure mode. Runtime was never the constraint: Bastrop ran in 107 seconds and Travis in 903. The statewide ADDRESS numbers are a genuine full-table measurement of all 253 loaded counties and are reported as such; statewide FIELD tallies do not exist and are not claimed.

findings.finding: The Tier-2 FEMA flood overlay reaches NO user on the production read path.
findings.evidence: 608,414 node-facets:tier2 rows hold flood determinations. mergeBakedBaseFacts composes its result from the atom response and never copies tier2 across, so the live body for 48021:36521 has no tier2 key at all while the store holds {status:in-sfha, floodZone:AO}. Asserted against captured LIVE bodies in live-parity.test.ts, not argued from code reading. Every flood-reading surface (compare-facts.ts:201, brief-verdict.ts:105, share-verdict.ts:50) therefore renders 'flood not verified here' for 100% of parcels.
findings.whyNoCoverageMetricSawIt: It is a SERVING drop, not a data gap. A store-side completeness ledger scores this rail 100% complete.

findings.finding: Two flood code paths hold DIFFERENT FEMA zones for the same parcel, and the disagreement tracks the NFHL snapshot each was baked from.
findings.evidence: 48021:36521 is zone AO in place_layer_snapshots tier2 (adapter fema:nfhl-flood-zone, vintage 2026-07-21) and AE on the flood-hazard-fact atom (adapter fema-nfhl-bulk-v1, vintage NFHL_48_20260101). Bastrop disagrees on 5,424 of 62,399 (8.69%) where both name a zone; Travis, where BOTH paths carry NFHL_48_20260101, disagrees on 332 of 804,458 (0.04%).
findings.consequence: This is the X-ray PDF defect the frozen contract quotes ('Zone AO on sheet 1, Flood zone AE on sheet 4') reproduced at source. Fixing F1 without reconciling the two stores ships a number that contradicts the other surface 8.69% of the time in Bastrop. SEQUENCE THE RECONCILIATION FIRST.

findings.finding: The address fix is a JOIN, not an acquisition — and it is a DIFFERENT join per county.
findings.evidence: Bastrop: the cad-parcel-roll atom for 48021:36521 carries situsAddress '1503 FARM ST', situsCity 'BASTROP', situsZip '78602'. It rides the served atom chain and adaptAtomChainToBakedFacets hardcodes baseFacts.situsAddress = null, so it is never read. 59,374 Bastrop parcels carry a street-segment situs on that roll, but only 1,036 of the 16,113 unreadable-address parcels intersect it (6.43%) — verified independently of the sweep by pulling both id sets and intersecting. Travis: cad-parcel-roll situsAddress is null on all 492,848 rows, so that path yields nothing; instead txgio_address holds '17005 SIMSBROOK DR', Pflugerville, 78660, with coordinates, vintage stratmap_address_points_48_most_recent. txgio_address holds 1,688,950 points across 6 counties (Bexar 710,316, Travis 433,031, Williamson 345,111, Hays 114,898, Bastrop 61,085, Caldwell 24,509), every one with a city, and nothing serves from it.

This is the operator's 'even places in Bastrop County saying it cant find setbacks', with every reason a named engineering decline rather than a mystery.

findings.finding: THIS LANE'S OWN FIRST PREDICATE MADE THE SAME MISTAKE AS THE 99.3% FIGURE.
findings.evidence: The first statewide pass used 'contains an alphanumeric' as the legibility rule and reported 94.64%. That rule passes the Travis-shaped stub ', TX 78754'. Corrected to a street-segment rule, the figure is 89.90%. Both numbers are published in the report. The ladder has three rungs so far — IS NOT NULL passes ', ,'; alphanumeric passes ', TX 78754'; street-segment is the current rule — and hasStreetSegment() states in source that there is no proof it has only three.

declaredDeviationsFromTheLivePath: No read-time calibration overlay (applyPropertyCalibrationAtRead) — a per-parcel read against a separate cortex-side table, seeded only for the Hays calibration set. Named in the resolverVersion string that travels with every record.

Envelope geojson replaced by a feature-count stand-in. Every read of geojson on the serving path is a null-ness test; proven behaviour-preserving in detectors-fire.test.ts and the parity test asserts the feature COUNT matches the live body.

The three transport failure branches (retrieval HTTP 401, transient upstream, JSON parse failure) are UNREACHABLE offline, so this sweep never emits `unresolved` from them. A zero unresolved count here is NOT evidence that the live path does not fail.
atomsByType and attachingRoads are assembled by the live chain and read by no consumer on this endpoint, so the sweep does not assemble them. An explicit scope boundary, not an omission.

whatRemainsOPEN: 252 of 254 counties are NOT swept. Statewide FIELD tallies do not exist and are not claimed anywhere. Runtime is not the obstacle (Bastrop 107s, Travis 903s); the reason to stop was that each new county changed how the numbers should be counted.

The absence-cluster grid is a fixed 0.05-degree grid, and for a field absent everywhere it reports parcel density rather than a finding. Stated in the report; a better shape would restrict clustering to fields with partial absence.

The zoning `no-zoning-stamp` class (52,700 in Bastrop, 147,671 in Travis) is classified absent-uncovered because the served reason is about OUR stamp coverage, not the world. Most unincorporated Texas is genuinely unzoned and that share is irreducible. The per-parcel reason token is preserved so the split can be made later without re-running the sweep, but the split has NOT been made.

The sweep measures ONE serving surface: the fact-sheet facets endpoint. The X-ray PDF, the site-plan sheets and the brief RE-DERIVE and were not swept; the report says the two zero contradiction counts relocate rather than clear that defect.
The vendor-drift control SKIPS without a hauska-map checkout, so it does not run on this repo's CI. It is a local pre-push control today.
PR #347 is open and unmerged by lane rule. CI conclusion string SUCCESS on head 73da2da.

Carry tier2 through mergeBakedBaseFacts so 608,414 baked flood determinations reach a user.
